concerns_addressed: Packet step-1 test intent writes `sort={column:'name',direction:'asc'}` while the spec's 'Table.tsx generic contract' section also says `direction`; the already-merged canonical T2 contract is `ColumnSort = { column, order }`. Implementation and tests follow the canonical `order` shape via `import type { ColumnSort } from '@/lib/admin-table'` — confirmed correct, no defect.
Diff range 62ce50e..79824b6 touches exactly the 3 in-scope files (Table.tsx M, Table.test.tsx A, index.ts M) — no API/pipeline/dummy/controller files in range.
Empty path (rows.length === 0) still returns `empty ?? <default copy>` with no `<thead>` — legacy contract intact.

Existing `Column<T>` = { key, header, render, className? } and `Props<T>` = { columns, rows, rowKey, empty? } are unchanged; all new props are optional, so the 6 not-yet-migrated pages keep compiling and rendering.

strengths: aria-sort mapping is exactly asc→"ascending", desc→"descending", otherwise/non-active sortable column→"none"; non-sortable columns get no aria-sort at all (`ariaSortValue` + `headerSort = sortable ? ... : undefined`, Table.tsx:36-39,70,74).

Non-sortable columns are genuinely inert: `onClick`, `onKeyDown` and `tabIndex` are all `sortable ? ... : undefined`, so the `Aksi` header has no handler at all — verified in code (Table.tsx:75-77) and by the test 'keeps non-sortable headers inert: clicking "Aksi" never calls onSort' (12/12 Table tests pass).

`density` and `sort` are optional and typed via `import type { ColumnSort, TableDensity } from '@/lib/admin-table'` — neither type is redefined locally; the barrel re-exports both with `export type` (index.ts:13), so no runtime coupling is introduced.

Density buckets map smaller/default/larger: compact px-5 py-2, default px-5 py-3 (th) / px-5 py-3.5 (td) — byte-equivalent to the pre-change legacy padding — and comfortable px-5 py-4 / px-5 py-5; `?? DENSITY_PADDING.default` guards a malformed runtime value.
Table stays generic: grep over Table.tsx finds no domain column name (`outlet`, `product`, `sku`, `created_at`, `role`, …); only `column.key`/`column.header` are used.
No pipeline/API/dummy files in the diff; `git diff --name-status` confirms 3 files only.
Backward-compat proven by execution: `npx jest src/app/admin` → 6 suites / 21 tests pass, and the full web suite → 27 suites / 159 tests pass; `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.

Refactor heuristics clean: Table.tsx 97 lines and Table.test.tsx 243 lines (both < ~300), the `Table` function is 46 lines (< ~50), no logic repeated 3+ times, and the two pure helpers (`ariaSortValue`, `SortIndicator`) are extracted.

Tests assert real behaviour (aria-sort tokens, arrow glyph, py-* padding tokens, onSort call args) rather than snapshots, and explicitly cover the no-`sortableColumns` inert fallback plus the legacy empty-state/rowKey contract.

issues.description: Additive keyboard path has zero test coverage: sortable <th> gains tabIndex={0} and an Enter/Space onKeyDown handler, but no test dispatches a key event, so the new behaviour is unverified. The DELIVERABLE only requires click-driven onSort, so this is an untested extra rather than a spec miss.

Comment accuracy: 'default MUST stay byte-identical to the legacy markup' is not literally true. For a non-sortable <th> the new class template yields an extra trailing space (the `${sortable ? ... : ''}` interpolation) versus the legacy single-space string. Purely cosmetic — browsers/CSS collapse class whitespace and no rendered style changes — and the padding tokens themselves are identical.
